title: Energy may run lower today.
caption: Energy may run lower today. Space is lively, with a fast solar wind and a south-tilted field, so a midday dip may land and screens can feel extra sharp. Keep tasks small and batch simple wins; eat on time, and add protein and a pinch of salt if you run low.
snapshot: Geomagnetic conditions are unsettled with a brisk solar wind and a southward-tilted magnetic field. No notable solar flares or eruptions were observed. This is a steady, active backdrop rather than a sharp spike.
affects: Low energy can show as an early battery dip or a midday sag that is hard to push through. Sensitivity-prone folks may also notice light and screen glare feeling heavier when the dip hits. Short, predictable routines tend to play nicer with this pattern.
playbook:
- Keep tasks bite-sized and batch simple wins
- Eat on time; add protein and salt if you run low
- Drink water through the day, not all at once
- Take brief outside breaks to reset your eyes
- Wrap the evening a little earlier if you can

Energy may run lower today. If you hit an early battery dip or that odd midday sag, you’re not imagining it—and screens may feel unkind right when the dip lands. Keep your to‑dos biteable and stack a couple of easy checkmarks at a time so your brain gets momentum without a fight.

Up above, the solar wind is moving quickly and the magnetic field is leaning south—more of a steady background push than a sudden jolt. Plan meals on schedule, and if you run low, add protein and a small pinch of salt to steady energy. Sip water through the day instead of chugging. Give your eyes a one‑minute outside lookaway between blocks; the distance reset can loosen that screen weight. If you can, close the evening a notch earlier to let your system catch up.
